newsitem.title: UK: UK's Sedgwick forms Columbia unit.
newsitem.headline: UK's Sedgwick forms Columbia unit.

text.p: British insurance firm Sedgwick Group Plc said on Monday that it had formed a new company in Columbia by joining up with two local partners.
Sedgwick will control 51 percent in the firm called Sedgwick Columbia Holdings, SA (SCH), it said in a statement.
The two other partners, Centurion Group and Cordel Limitada, would control 24.5 percent in the venture, the statement said.
Robin Romer-Lee, director of Sedgwick's Latin American affairs, told Reuters that SCH expected to start business in Columbia around February 1997 with an employee strength 56.
"We see a huge opportunity there, in an opening economy," Romer Lee said. Private company pensions and healthcare benefits would be the initial thrust areas, he said.

SCH would become the owner of three Centurion trading companies and would also apply to the Columbian Banking Superintendency for permsision to form a new reinsurance subsidiary. "The book value of the net assets to be acquired is less than 150,000 stg," Sedgwick's statement said.
Romer-Lee said SCH would become the third largest reinsurance broker and one of the largest retail insurance brokers in Columbia.
